sections.h2: Third-party cover is 59 per cent of motor premium, the long-tail half

chart.title: Third-party cover is the larger motor line, and the one that holds float
chart.source: General Insurance Council segment-wise return, provisional and unaudited.

sections.means: Third-party claims settle over one to three years or longer, so the insurer holds the premium for that long.
sections.todo: Read motor float from the third-party line, not from total motor premium.

sections.h2: Berkshire's insurance arm holds $294 billion of equities against $17 billion of bonds

chart.title: Same float, opposite portfolios: Berkshire's insurance assets lean to equity
chart.sub: Berkshire insurance operations at 31 December 2025, $ billion.

sections.means: Berkshire's float is invested mainly in equities, while Indian general insurers must hold mostly government paper.
sections.todo: Compare insurers' portfolios against their own statutory floors, not against Berkshire's.

sections.h2: Statutory floors force most of an Indian insurer's portfolio into government paper

chart.title: A general insurer must hold at least 20 per cent in central government securities
chart.sub: Minimum share of the investment portfolio, %, under the Insurance Act.
chart.source: Insurance Act as administered by IRDAI.

sections.means: A general insurer must hold at least 20 per cent central government securities and 30 per cent approved securities.
sections.todo: Check an insurer's statutory floors before assuming it can hold equities the way Berkshire does.
